annotation.title_clean: The Human Control Over Autonomous Robotic Systems: What Ethical and Legal Lessons for Judicial Uses of AI?
annotation.title_en: The Human Control Over Autonomous Robotic Systems: What Ethical and Legal Lessons for Judicial Uses of AI?
annotation.venue: Book chapter (ISBN 9783030666361), deposited in IRIS UNICA (University of Cagliari)
annotation.summary_en: Book chapter (repository abstract page) examining normative problems of increasingly autonomous robotic systems through two case studies, autonomous weapons and autonomous surgical robots, to draw lessons on shared human-machine control, acceptability of autonomous decisions, and human responsibility for harms, applied to judicial uses of AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous weapons systems raise the issue of acceptability of autonomous decision-making in ethically and legally sensitive domains
Increasingly autonomous surgical robots raise the issue of human responsibility for harms caused by autonomous agents
The shared control relationship between human and machine is central to governing autonomous systems
Lessons from robotics apply to the judge-software relationship in judicial AI
